description: Eleventh held-out set: twenty-seven tasks, three per target skill, written after the tenth set was frozen and never tuned against. Each has an organic prompt, judge-only criteria, and a hidden acceptance check under holdout-v11-checks/ that the agent never sees.

claim.prompt: Bramble got up to 640 g when we weighed her on the 14th, but `npm run ready` in agent-suites/fixtures/hedgehog-rescue still has her at 585 g and not ready. I think it isn't picking up anything from the last week or so, like it's working off an old copy of the weigh-ins. We want to let a few go this weekend before it turns cold, so could you sort it out?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: latestWeighIn() in src/release.mjs sorts the dates as text, and the tablet writes them day first without padding (14/10/2026, 3/10/2026) while the office PC writes 2026-10-07. As text '14/10/2026' sorts before every '2026-…' date, so Bramble's latest comes out as 7 October (585 g).

The stale-copy theory is checked and rejected with evidence: recent weigh-ins are read (Hazel's 655 g on 15 October, six days old, is used), and the weigh-in picked for Bramble is neither the oldest nor a cached value but the last of the PC-format dates.

Other hogs are found, and the dangerous one is flagged: Pip shows 615 g and ready from a tablet reading on 30/9/2026, but her real latest weigh-in is 570 g on 13 October, so she would have been released underweight. Conker, weighed only on the tablet, shows 575 g but is really 630 g, and Juniper's latest is 530 g, not 480 g.

The second fault is found: releaseStatus() tests `grams > 600`, but the README says at least 600 g, so Thistle at exactly 600 g is held back. After fixing only the dates, Thistle still shows not ready, and the reply says so or fixes it.

The fix reads both date forms in code as day-first dates (new Date('9/10/2026') reads it as 10 September, and '14/10/2026' as an invalid date, so a plain Date parse is wrong), with regression tests for a mixed PC and tablet history and for 600 g exactly. Rewriting data/hogs.json alone is weaker, since the tablet keeps writing that format.

`npm run ready` is rerun and shows Hazel, Bramble, Thistle, Conker and Sorrel ready and Pip, Juniper and Moss (599 g) not ready. The reply names the hogs the report missed, warns that Pip is not ready, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: Mrs Patel's been on the phone: Biscuit's groom on the 14th was his sixth with us, so it should have been his free one, but `npm run bill -- 2026-10` in agent-suites/fixtures/dog-grooming charges her £43 for it. I think the loyalty count is starting again every month instead of carrying on. Can you fix it before I send October's bills out?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: priceGrooms() in src/prices.mjs counts grooms by the dog's name exactly as stored, and Biscuit's 2 September booking came through the online form as owner 'patel', dog 'biscuit', so it is counted as a different dog and the 14 October groom comes out as his 5th.

The monthly-reset theory is checked and rejected with evidence: the bill shows Biscuit's groom as number 5, not 1 or 2, and Luna's free 6th groom on 9 September was counted from grooms in July and August.

Other affected dogs are found in both directions: Pepper (Ashby), whose online bookings were saved as 'Pepper ' and 'pepper', should get her free 6th groom on 22 October but is charged £44; and Max (Hughes) and Max (Jones), two different dogs, are counted together by name, so Max Hughes got a free groom on 2 October that was really only his 3rd. Keying on the dog's name, even trimmed and lower-cased, still merges the two Maxes.

The second fault is found: a free groom is priced at £0 including its extras, but the README says extras are still charged. Once the count is fixed Biscuit comes out at £0, not the £5 for his nail clip; Rocco's free groom on 6 October dropped his £8 flea bath, and Luna's free groom in September dropped her £5 nail clip on a bill already sent. The reply notes that this is not quite 'free' as Mrs Patel expects.

The fix counts grooms per owner and dog with names trimmed and compared without case, in code, and charges extras on the free groom, with regression tests for an online-form name, two same-named dogs and a free groom with extras.

`npm run bill -- 2026-10` is rerun and shows Biscuit at £5.00, Pepper at £6.00 and Rocco at £8.00 as free grooms, Max Hughes at £30.00 (groom 3) and £35.00, Max Jones £46.00 (groom 4) and a total of £225.00 rather than £263.00. The reply names the customers the report missed, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: Our October Gift Aid claim in agent-suites/fixtures/lifeboat-donations is missing Derek Penrose's £50. He definitely has a declaration, he filled in the online form on the 20th after we asked him. He paid by bank transfer, and I think the claim only picks up card and cash donations, because the bank ones come in on a separate export. Can you fix it so I can send the claim off?

criteria: The cause is shown with output, not guessed: findDeclaration() in src/giftaid.mjs compares postcodes exactly, and Penrose's online declaration saved his postcode as 'tr18 4aa' while his donations say 'TR18 4AA', so none of them match. His £10 card donation on 25 October, made after he signed, is missing too.
The bank-transfer theory is checked and rejected with evidence: nothing in the code looks at the method, and Jenny Hosking's and Ruth Pascoe's bank transfers are already claimed (£10.00 and £25.00).

The second fault is found: covers() rejects any donation made before the declaration was signed, but the README says a declaration covers the four years before it. After fixing only the postcode, Penrose's £50 on 9 October is still not claimed, since he signed on the 20th, and the reply says so or fixes it. Mary Kitto's £20 on 2 October (signed 15 October) is missed for the same reason.

Other affected donations are found: Sue Angove's donations carry the postcode 'TR194PL' from the card reader, so her £25 in October and her £25 in September are unclaimed, and Penrose's £20 in September is unclaimed too. The September claim is short by £11.25, and the reply flags that as money that can still be claimed, not just a side note.

The fix is in code: postcodes compared without case or spaces, and cover starting on the same date four years before signing (not 4 × 365 days), while Alan Rowse's 18 October donation, after he cancelled on the 10th, stays unclaimed. Regression tests cover a differently typed postcode and a donation made before the declaration was signed. Rewriting the data alone is weaker, since the online form and card reader keep producing those forms.

`npm run claim -- 2026-10` and `npm run claim -- 2026-09` are rerun: October claims £71.75 on £332.00 rather than £45.50, with Penrose at £12.50 and £2.50, Kitto £5.00 and Angove £6.25, and September claims £21.25 rather than £10.00. The reply names the donors the report missed, and its claims match what was run.

claim.prompt: Since we imported all the old branch spreadsheets into the village society mailing list in agent-suites/fixtures/newsletter-list, the merge step has become painfully slow: `npm run perf` shows a median of roughly 680 ms, and the membership page reruns it on every edit. Please get it under 10 ms. The merged list decides who gets the newsletter and who has unsubscribed, so it has to come out exactly as it does now, entry for entry. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 680 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 10 ms with errors at zero and the same work (1600 entries from 3200 rows, 1405 to mail). Behaviour is identical: addresses compared after trimming and lower-casing, Gmail and googlemail.com treated as one with dots and `+` suffixes ignored only there (plus addresses on other providers stay separate), rows with no usable address (empty, missing, no dot in the domain, two @) each kept as their own invalid entry and never merged with each other, the first-written address and first non-blank name kept, tags merged ignoring case with the first spelling and blanks dropped, the earliest join date kept with a missing first date left missing as the plain `<` comparison does, any unsubscribe sticking, and first-appearance order. The caller's rows are not changed and each call returns fresh entries.

The fix is the single change the profile points to (indexing entries by mailbox in a Map within the call) rather than a rewrite of the address rules; anything tried that did not help is reverted, and each kept change is its own commit with its measured effect.

The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: mergeSubscribers() searches the whole merged list with `list.find` for every row and re-runs the regular expression in mailbox() on every existing entry each time, which is quadratic in the number of rows. Indexing entries by their mailbox once per call is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: At the night championship the results screen in agent-suites/fixtures/orienteering-results lagged badly once all four courses were downloading: `npm run perf` gives a median of around 340 ms and the screen refreshes after every card that comes in. Can you get it under 30 ms? Prizes and the split tables come from these results, so places, times and leg ranks have to stay exactly as they are now. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 340 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 30 ms with errors at zero and the same work (1280 runners, 1215 finishers, 22183 leg times, the same four winners). Behaviour is identical: controls found greedily in course order among the punches (repeats and stray punches allowed), no finish (null or missing) is DNF even with every control punched, a missing control is MP, clocks earlier than the start count as the next day and stray spaces are ignored, equal times share a place and the next is skipped, leg ranks count only strictly faster finishers on that course so ties share a rank, MP and DNF runners keep the legs they completed with no rank and do not affect anyone else's rank, finishers come before MP before DNF with names by `localeCompare` then bib, unknown courses are left out and empty courses still listed. The caller's data is not changed.

After the first improvement the agent re-measures and re-profiles rather than stopping or repeating the same idea: the second, different bottleneck is found and fixed, and each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted.

The reply reports baseline, each step's number, final number, spread and what dominated the cost at each stage: first the sort comparator calling analyse() (which parses every clock through `new Date`) for both runners on every comparison; once each runner is analysed once, the remaining cost is places and leg ranks found by filtering every finisher for every runner and every leg, which is quadratic per leg. Ranking against each leg's finisher times sorted once (counting strictly smaller values) is the expected shape of the second fix.

claim.prompt: The members' page for our boat syndicate (agent-suites/fixtures/boat-syndicate) has got really sluggish now that four seasons of trips and bills are in: `npm run perf` puts the statements at about 470 ms median, and they're recalculated every time anyone opens the page. Can you get that under 10 ms? People pay what their statement says, so every penny has to come out exactly as it does now. You're on a branch, so commit as you go.

criteria: The timing script and its data are unchanged, a baseline (about 470 ms) is recorded before any change, and results come from repeated runs with their spread.

The median is under 10 ms with errors at zero and the same work (3360 lines, 3996493p billed, the same twelve totals). Behaviour is identical: each trip rounded to a tenth of an hour on its own before summing (not summed in floating point then rounded), guests' trips ignored, periods inclusive at both ends, a period with no hours falling back to shares (not equal) among members aboard, shares and equal splits only among members whose membership overlaps the period (everyone if nobody does), whole pence by floor plus largest remainder with earlier members winning ties, and negative costs split with the same floor rule. The caller's members, trips and costs are not sorted or changed.

No result or intermediate (usage per member and period, parsed trips, a memo keyed by the trips array or by ids and dates) is kept between calls: the books are changed in place between page views, so anything remembered across calls would show stale statements. The speed-up comes from doing the work once per call, and the agent says why a cross-call cache, though it would make the timing script look instant, is wrong here. Rounding shortcuts that only approximately match are not used.

Each kept improvement is its own commit with its measured effect; changes that did not help are reverted rather than kept. The reply reports baseline, final number, spread and what dominated the cost: for every hours cost, usage() filters every trip once per member and parses three dates with `Date.parse` for each trip it looks at. Reading the trips once per call (grouped by member with dates parsed once, optionally with running totals for a binary search per period) is the expected shape of the fix.

claim.prompt: The pumpkin farm in agent-suites/fixtures/pumpkin-patch works out prices in three separate places: the barn till (bin/till.mjs), the receipt reprints (bin/receipts.mjs) and the click-and-collect quotes (src/online-orders.mjs). Every time the rates change somebody forgets one of them. Please pull the pricing into src/pricing.mjs with a single rate table that all three use, and get rid of the copies. This is a tidy-up, not a price change: the till, the receipts, the online quotes and the price board on the barn wall have to print exactly what they print today, and nothing that uses this package should notice.

criteria: The copies are compared before they are merged, and the differences are kept rather than smoothed over: the online copy charges at least 200p per pumpkin; the receipt copy falls back to the carving rate for a missing or unknown variety where the till refuses it; the two copies word their errors differently; and the online copy multiplies by pounds per kilo, which rounds differently for whole-kilo giant pumpkins (13kg is £11.10 at the till and £11.00 online, 21kg is £17.90 and £17.80). Any merged formula reproduces each channel's figure for those weights.

Every user of the old tables is found, including the one a search of the .mjs files misses: scripts/board.sh (the `npm run board` price board) imports RATES from bin/till.mjs inside a `node -e` one-liner, so it either keeps working through bin/till.mjs or is pointed at src/pricing.mjs.

The package's outside name is kept: package.json exports `./orders` to src/online-orders.mjs for the web shop, so `quoteOrder` stays exported there with the same results and the same error for a variety the shop does not sell.
There is one rate table, in src/pricing.mjs, used by the till, the receipts and the online quotes, with no second table in pounds left behind; the tests are updated where needed and pass.

Output is shown to be identical by capturing every command (till with several weights and bad input, receipts and online quotes for more than the bundled files, the board) before and after, and the reply names the differences between the copies, says how each was kept, and flags the till and online disagreement on giant pumpkins as something the farm may want to decide on separately.

claim.prompt: The workshop in agent-suites/fixtures/clock-repair now calls rush jobs "priority" jobs, but the code still says "urgent" everywhere and new staff keep asking about it. Please rename it inside the code: src/urgent.mjs becomes src/priority.mjs, isUrgent, urgentDueDate and urgentQueue become isPriority, priorityDueDate and priorityQueue, and the `urgent` field on job objects becomes `priority`. Update the tests and don't keep the old names around as aliases. Leave data/jobs.json and config/shop.json alone: the booking tablet writes the first and the accounts spreadsheet reads the second. Nobody at the bench, at the counter or at the insurer should notice anything.

criteria: Every use is found, including the ones a search for `.urgent` or `isUrgent` misses: src/invoice.mjs switches surcharges on by the string field name in SURCHARGES and builds both the config key (`${kind}SurchargePence`) and the invoice line ("Urgent surcharge") from it; bin/queue.mjs declares the option as `urgent` and src/args.mjs turns option names into flags, so renaming it renames `--urgent`; and bin/export.mjs spreads the whole job into the insurer's CSV, so renaming the field renames the `urgent` column.

The outside names are deliberately kept: the `--urgent` flag, the `urgentSurchargePence` and `urgentTurnaroundDays` config keys, the "URGENT" and "Urgent surcharge" wording, and the `urgent` column (in the same position) in the export. Inside the code only the new names remain, with no fallback or alias, and src/urgent.mjs is gone.

The two different ideas of a rush job are kept apart rather than merged into isPriority: the queue and due dates count only `true`, while the invoice charges the surcharge for any truthy value, so J-1043 (`"yes"` from the old tablet) is charged but not queued first. The tablet's raw value is carried through to the export unchanged, and a job with no `urgent` field gets no `priority` key or column added.

The tablet's field is translated at the edges (on load, and back for the export) keeping each record's key order and extra fields, so the output is the same for a job book whose fields come in another order.

Output is shown to be identical by capturing every command (queue with and without --urgent and --date, every invoice, the export, an unknown option and a missing job) before and after, for more than the bundled job book; the tests are updated and pass, and the reply lists each migrated site, which outside names were kept and why, and points out the `"yes"` disagreement as something to settle separately.

claim.prompt: src/hire.mjs in agent-suites/fixtures/skip-hire has turned into everything at once. Please move the council permit side out into its own module, src/permits.mjs: PERMIT_FEES, needsPermit, permitFee, permitEnd, expiringPermits and permitApplication. Skip sizes, councils, delivery and quotes stay in hire.mjs. Point the code at the new module rather than going through hire.mjs. While you're in there, bin/letters.mjs has its own copy of needsPermit, so have it use the shared one if it's the same rule. What matters most is that nobody can tell anything changed: every command, the letters included, has to print exactly what it prints now. If some part of this can't be done without changing what gets printed, leave that part as it is and tell me why.

criteria: Every user of the moved names is found, including the ones a search for import lines in .mjs files misses: bin/quote.mjs prices each part by building the function name (`hire[`${part}Fee`]`) from data/quote-parts.json, so a moved permitFee would make every quote fail with "Nothing prices the permit part"; and ops/permit-reminders.sh, the cron job, imports expiringPermits from src/hire.mjs inside a `node -e` one-liner.

The outside name is kept: package.json exports `./hire` and the README says the councils' permit portal calls needsPermit and permitFee from `skip-hire/hire`, so those stay available there with the same answers (a re-export or an export-map entry), and the reply says why that exception to "not through hire.mjs" was made.

The letters copy is compared before it is replaced, and is found not to be the same rule: it sends letters for anything that is not a driveway or private ground (verges, pavements, a missing placement), while needsPermit is only `road`. Switching letters to the shared needsPermit would drop the letters for SK-313 and other verge skips, so the agent keeps the letters behaviour (for example under its own name) and raises the conflict instead of silently changing who gets a letter.

src/permits.mjs defines all six moved names and hire.mjs no longer defines them; any import cycle between the two modules (permits needs councilFor and SIZES, quotes need permitFee) is safe for either module loading first; quotes, permit applications and reminders go through the new module; the tests are updated and pass.

Output is shown to be identical by capturing each command (quotes for each booking and for ad-hoc skips including unknown sizes and postcodes, letters, permit applications, and the reminder script for several dates) before and after, and the reply lists each migrated site, including the name-built lookup and the cron script.

claim.prompt: Every Tuesday at agent-suites/fixtures/soup-kitchen we guess how many bowls to put out and either run short or wash fifty for nothing, so I'd like the project to work it out from the batches. First add `parseVolume(text)` in src/volume.mjs that turns a pot as the cooks write it into millilitres. A volume is whole millilitres (`750ml`), litres with up to two decimal places (`20l`, `18.5l`, `0.75l`), or whole pints (`1 pint`, `6 pints`), and a pint counts as 568 ml. Units can be any case, it's `pint` for exactly one and `pints` for any other number, and there's at most one space between the number and its unit. Numbers have no leading zeros apart from the single 0 in something like `0.75l`. A volume has to be more than nothing and no more than 50 litres, which is our biggest pot. Anything else throws a RangeError quoting the text, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--servings <date>` to `npm run batches`. Leave out burnt batches, add up each soup's volume across that day's batches (soup names match whatever their case), and print one line per soup that has any, in the order of data/soups.json: the soup's name as it is in that file, two spaces, the day's volume, two spaces, then how many 300 ml bowls it gives once 5% is lost to the ladle and the bottom of the pots, counting only full bowls, like `41 bowls` (`1 bowl` for one). Volumes under a litre show like `750 ml` and from a litre up like `18.5 l`, with up to three decimals and no trailing zeros (`5 l`). Finish with `Batches: <n>`, the number of batches counted. A pot that can't be read, or a batch of a soup we don't make, is left out and reported on stderr with its batch id and the pot or the soup as it was written, and the command still exits 0. If nothing was cooked that day, or all of it was burnt, print `Nothing to serve on <date>.` The date has to be a real date written exactly as YYYY-MM-DD; otherwise, or if it's missing, say what's wrong on stderr and exit 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `soup: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: each of the three volume shapes in any case with and without the single space, 1 ml, exactly 50 l in each shape and just over it (`50001ml`, `50.01l`, 89 pints against 88), decimals beyond two places, `.5l` and `5.l`, leading zeros (`020l`, `00.5l`, `01 pint`), zero in every shape, `1 pints` and `2 pint`, fractional pints and millilitres, doubled or surrounding spaces, signs, exponents, hex, commas, Infinity, non-string values, and the CLI's 3 November list (burnt S43 left out, lower-case `carrot and coriander`, `2.01L` read as 2010 ml where `2.01 * 1000` gives 2009.999…, Leek and Potato's 160 bowls from the day's 50.59 l where flooring each batch gives 159, a day's total above the 50 l pot limit, Tomato's `1 bowl`, the S45, S46 and S47 problems on stderr), the 10 November `0 bowls` line, the nothing-to-serve day, a leap day, and the exit-2 dates.

The implementation is small (one pattern per volume shape, or one combined pattern, and integer millilitre arithmetic for the decimals and the 5%) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example `50.00l`, `0.0l`, a soup whose volume fills no bowl, a batch whose every pot is unreadable, whether a batch of an unknown soup counts towards `Batches:`, a soup listed twice in data/soups.json, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --servings, the volume notation and the bowl rule, and the volume rules live in one place.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and the 3 November servings list.

claim.prompt: I do the summer ladder for agent-suites/fixtures/gliding-club by hand from the launch point sheets and I've got it wrong twice this year, so please teach the project to score a task day. First add `parseElapsed(text)` in src/elapsed.mjs. An elapsed time is minutes and two-digit seconds (`47:12`) for anything under an hour, or hours, two-digit minutes and two-digit seconds (`2:30:25`) from an hour up. The first number has no leading zero (a single `0` is fine, as in `0:58`), the minutes in the short form are under 60, and every two-digit part is under 60. It returns the time in seconds, which has to be more than nothing and under eight hours, when the launch point closes. `DNF`, `DNS` and `DSQ` in any case return that code in capitals. Anything else throws a RangeError quoting the text, and anything that isn't a string throws a TypeError. Then add `--results <task id>` to `npm run tasks`. A pilot's handicapped time is their elapsed time × their glider's index from data/handicaps.json ÷ 100, rounded to the nearest second with half a second going up; glider types match whatever their case. List the finishers fastest handicapped time first, alphabetically by pilot on a tie, one line each: the place, two spaces, the pilot's name and the glider type as written in data/handicaps.json in brackets, two spaces, the handicapped time written the same way as elapsed times, two spaces and the points. Points are the place, except that pilots on the same handicapped time share the place, written with an `=` in front (`=3`), and each gets the average of the places they cover, so two pilots on `=3` score 3.5 each and the next pilot is 5th. After the finishers come the pilots with a code, in the order they're on the sheet: the code, two spaces, the pilot and glider as above, two spaces and the points, where DNF and DSQ score one more than the number of pilots who launched (everyone but DNS) and DNS scores one more than the number of pilots entered. Finish with `Launched: <launched> of <entered>`. A pilot whose glider type has no handicap, or whose time can't be read, is left out of the results and the counts and reported on stderr with their name and the glider or time as it was written, and the command still exits 0. The task id should match whatever the case, ignoring spaces around it. A missing or unknown id says so on stderr and exits 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `glide: `.

criteria: Tests are written before or alongside the code and pin the public behaviour: both time shapes, one second, `59:59` against `1:00:00`, `7:59:59` against `8:00:00`, `0:58` against `00:58` and `0:47:12`, short-form minutes of 60 or more (`61:10`), one-digit or three-digit parts (`47:5`, `2:7:15`), parts of 60, decimals, signs, exponents, surrounding or inner spaces, extra colons, look-alike codes (`DNFF`, `RET`, ` DNF`), each code in mixed case, non-string values, and the CLI's T7 results (Kim Ng's 8483.5 s rounding up to 2:21:24, lower-case `ls8`, Ann Lee and Ruth Okafor tied on `=3` in alphabetical order with 3.5 points and Mo Tan 5th, DNF and DSQ on 9 and DNS on 10 in sheet order, Ivy Rose's unknown `Discus`, Tom Fox's and Bea Kerr's unreadable times on stderr and out of the counts), the all-DNS T8 with `Launched: 0 of 2`, T9's `0:59` and over-eight-hour handicapped time, and the exit-2 ids.

The implementation is small (one pattern per time shape, integer arithmetic for the half-up rounding, one pass that groups equal times) and decides unspecified cases deliberately and names them in the reply (for example three or more pilots tied, a handicapped time that goes past eight hours, a pilot entered twice, a handicap index that isn't a positive whole number, a task day with no finishers, the place shown for pilots after a tie, and the exact stderr wording).
Without the option the list is unchanged, the README documents --results, the time notation and the scoring rules, and the time rules live in one place used for reading and writing times.
The work was checked against the request before reporting, issues found were fixed, and the reply shows the tests passing and the T7 results.

claim.prompt: The office at agent-suites/fixtures/storage-units chases late rent from a paper diary and keeps getting the late fees wrong, so I'd like the project to work out who owes what. Add `arrears(unit, today)` in src/arrears.mjs, where `today` is a date written YYYY-MM-DD, returning `{ months, fees, total }` in pence. Rent is due every month on the unit's `dueDay`, and in a month that doesn't have that day it's due on the month's last day instead, so a unit due on the 31st pays on 30 April and 28 February and still on 31 March. Every due date from `firstUnpaid` up to and including `today` is owed (`months` is how many), and each one adds the rent plus a late fee: nothing for the first 7 days after the due date, then £5 for each week or part of a week after that, up to £30 for that month. `total` is the rent owed plus the fees. A unit with `firstUnpaid: null` owes nothing. A unit has to have `rent` as a whole number of pence above 0, `dueDay` a whole number from 1 to 31, and `firstUnpaid` either null or a real date written YYYY-MM-DD that is one of that unit's due dates. A unit that breaks these throws a RangeError naming the unit's id, a `today` that isn't a real date written that way throws a RangeError quoting it, and a unit that isn't an object throws a TypeError. Then add `--arrears <date>` to `npm run units`. Print one line for each unit that owes anything on that date, most owed first and by unit id when two owe the same: the unit id, two spaces, the tenant, two spaces, the months owed like `3 months` (`1 month` for one), two spaces and the total like `£185.00`. Finish with `Total  £1315.00`, the sum of the lines, or if nobody owes anything print `No arrears on <date>.` instead. A unit that breaks the rules is named on stderr and left out, and the command still exits 0. The date has to be a real date written exactly as YYYY-MM-DD; otherwise, or if it's missing, say what's wrong on stderr and exit 2 with nothing on stdout. Everything the command writes to stderr starts with `store: `.
